lesson_title: Why His Savings Jar Stayed Empty for Three Months
hook_text: He tried to save for three months and ended up with almost nothing. One change fixed it.
clip_script: Sipho wants a R600 school bag. Every month he saves what is left. Every month: nothing. Where did it go? A cooldrink every day, R200. Extra data, R80. Friday kotas with friends, R100. Small wants, peer pressure, no plan. So he flips it: pay yourself first. Payday, R100 straight into the jar, then spend. Cooldrink twice a week. Kotas once a month. Half of every odd-job payment saved. End of November: R640. Bag bought, R40 to start the next goal. Save for emergencies, goals and the future, and pay yourself first.
visual_style: A whiteboard jar staying empty while coins leak out to cooldrinks and kotas, then the jar filling as coins drop in first on payday.
pacing: A quick problem, a detective look at the leaks, then a satisfying fill-up.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and set your own pay-yourself-first amount.
